nodes.name: Webhook
nodes.notes: Contract matches publishToTikTok() in services/socialService.ts: { branch_id (UUID), caption, media_type: video|image|carousel, media_urls: string[], scheduled_for }. TikTok has NO text-only post -- media_urls is always required.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ success: false, error: 'Missing required fields: branch_id and caption are required' }) }}

nodes.name: Fetch TikTok Credentials
nodes.notes: After importing, RE-ATTACH the Header Auth credential here (apikey = Hub service_role key). n8n links credentials by name, so imports arrive dangling and every publish fails with n8n's generic 'Credentials not found' before any logic runs.

nodes.name: Query Creator Info
nodes.notes: TikTok REQUIRES this before any direct post. It returns the privacy levels this account may actually use, plus comment/duet/stitch locks that we must honour.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ media_type: 'PHOTO', post_mode: 'DIRECT_POST', post_info: { title: $json.title, description: $json.description, privacy_level: $json.privacy_level, disable_comment: $json.disable_comment, auto_add_music: true, brand_organic_toggle: true }, source_info: { source: 'PULL_FROM_URL', photo_images: $json.media_urls, photo_cover_index: 0 } }) }}

nodes.name: Init Photo Post
nodes.notes: Photos are PULL_FROM_URL ONLY -- there is no file-upload path for images. That makes TikTok URL-ownership verification mandatory: the image host must be a domain we have verified in the TikTok developer portal. Supabase Storage lives on supabase.co, which we cannot verify, so photo posts fail with 403 url_ownership_unverified until media is served from a domain we own.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ post_info: { title: $json.title, privacy_level: $json.privacy_level, disable_comment: $json.disable_comment, disable_duet: $json.disable_duet, disable_stitch: $json.disable_stitch, brand_organic_toggle: true }, source_info: { source: 'PULL_FROM_URL', video_url: $json.media_urls[0] } }) }}

nodes.name: Init Video Post
nodes.notes: PULL_FROM_URL requires a verified URL. If URL verification is not in place, switch source_info to FILE_UPLOAD (video only) -- that path needs no domain verification but must chunk the bytes (5-64MB per chunk).

nodes.name: Wait Before Status Check
nodes.notes: 15s. TikTok allows only 6 requests per minute per user token, shared with the init call -- a tighter loop trips 429 rate_limit_exceeded.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ event_type: 'social_publish', source: 'tiktok', payload: { branch_id: $json.branch_id, post_id: $json.post_id, caption: $json.caption, platform: 'tiktok', media_type: $json.media_type, privacy_level: $json.privacy_level, published_at: new Date().toISOString() } }) }}

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ success: true, post_id: $('Interpret Status').first().json.post_id, privacy_level: $('Interpret Status').first().json.privacy_level, message: $('Interpret Status').first().json.privacy_level === 'SELF_ONLY' ? 'Published to TikTok as PRIVATE (SELF_ONLY) - the app has not passed TikTok content-posting audit' : 'Published successfully to TikTok' }) }}

nodes.name: Success Response
nodes.notes: Reads from Interpret Status BY NAME, not $json: Log Marketing Event sits in between and its HTTP response would otherwise replace $json (the bug that returned null post ids from the Instagram publisher on 2026-08-01).

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ success: false, error: $json.error, code: $json.code || null, needs_review: $json.needs_review || false }) }}

nodes.name: Error Response
nodes.notes: HTTP 200 with success:false is deliberate -- a bare non-200 collapses every distinct failure into 'Webhook returned 500' for the caller.

parameters.content:
## Trellis: TikTok Publisher

Serves **`trellis-tiktok-publish`** for `publishToTikTok()` and the S1 scheduler.

### Setup after import
1. **Fetch TikTok Credentials** -> re-attach the Header Auth credential
   (`apikey` = Hub service_role key). Imports always arrive dangling.
2. **Log Marketing Event** -> confirm the `Sproutify Trellis` Supabase credential.
3. Activate. Also import and activate **T1-tiktok-token-refresh.json** -- TikTok
   access tokens expire every 24 HOURS, so without it publishing dies daily.

### TWO EXTERNAL BLOCKERS (not fixable in code)
1. **App audit.** Until the TikTok app passes the Content Posting API audit,
   every post is forced to `SELF_ONLY` (private), the posting account itself must
   be private, and only 5 users may post per 24h. A public attempt returns 403
   `unaudited_client_can_only_post_to_private_accounts`. This workflow surfaces
   the forced privacy level in its success message rather than pretending.
2. **URL ownership verification.** TikTok fetches media by URL and only accepts
   URLs on a domain verified in the developer portal. Supabase Storage is on
   `supabase.co`, which we do not control and cannot DNS-verify. Serve media from
   a domain we own (e.g. `media.sproutify.app` proxying Storage -- it must return
   the bytes with 200, NOT a 302 redirect, which TikTok rejects).
   Photos are PULL_FROM_URL only. Video could instead use FILE_UPLOAD, which
   needs no verification but must chunk the bytes.

### Flow
validate -> credential -> creator_info (mandatory) -> choose privacy from the
account's real options -> init (photo or video) -> poll status every 15s up to
~2 min -> published / failed / needs_review.

Polling is bounded because TikTok allows only **6 requests per minute** per user
token. A timeout answers `needs_review`, never a retry -- retrying risks a
double post.
